parsed.answer: This has been reported before. Square brackets in the path are treated as wildcards by Windows PowerShell 5.1 when it sets its starting location, so it falls back to C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0 (or, per #19595, wt launched from such a path can land in the home directory). This is a known bug in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and is tracked in terminal#11149, not something Terminal can fix. The past tickets say the fix is to use PowerShell 7+ (pwsh) instead: install it and set it as the profile used for wt.exe and 'Open in Terminal' in File Explorer, or set it as your default profile. Note that #19595 reports that with PowerShell 7.5.4 launched via wt.exe the directory was still reset to the home directory, but that was without a starting directory set for the profile, which Terminal does not inherit from the parent process. If your issue persists in PowerShell 7 when --startingDirectory is passed explicitly, add that detail (shell version and exact command) to the existing tickets.
